items.title: Bobby Shew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 1, 2020
items.q: And the contractor was Gus Klein who was Manny Klein’s son. You know? And Gus is a good guy but Gus leans over and he says, “Bobby, what the hell are you doing?”

ctx.x: Oh that’s a good one. You don’t find — they don’t teach you that in music school.

No they don’t. So I was doing a thing at Universal Studios one day and it was just sort of like a silly movie about like the late 20s or early 30s or something. And it was a scene where there was a little kind of a John Philip Sousa tiny band on a gazebo in a park and people were all walking through on a Sunday afternoon you know, and they’re dressed up and all of that. And you turn the page and there’s “Carnival of Venice.” What? Why the writer had to put that there. He could have put anything there, but this…

things. Sometimes, and I got caught one time on a film, a TV movie about some inconsequential invasion of bees in an Indiana small village. Who knew? It was not important but there was only one trumpet on the thing and I turned the page and there was a whole bunch of double tonguing. And I tried to do it and I really couldn’t do it. I could not handle it. And I went oh, and you’ve got 30 seconds to get it ready. And so I did it one time and it was terrible. And the conductor goes, “Take two.” Oh you want to hear…
